newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa stable, keen to return home.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa stable, keen to return home.

text.p: Mother Teresa was doing well on Wednesday as she recovered from a fall and wanted to go home, doctors treating the legendary Roman Catholic missionary said.
"Mother Teresa is doing well, still it was decided to keep her under observation for a few more days," a medical bulletin said.
Doctors said Mother Teresa continued to have an irregular heart beat, which she has suffered since her stay in the hospital in late August and early September.
"Her cardiac condition remains unchanged," the bulletin said.
The six-member medical team looking after Mother Teresa was expanded on Wednesday by the inclusion of a neurologist and a nephrologist, hospital authorities said.
Mother Teresa, 86, was admitted to the hospital on Monday after falling from a chair.
Doctors said they would do another brain scan to check a suspected spot found on her brain.
"We are ascertaining whether the black spot detected in the brain scan was from her old injury," said Dr Dinamani Banerjee, who examined Mother Teresa on Wednesday morning.
"We will have another CAT (brain) scan in a couple of days to confirm whether it is insignificant and we are not releasing her for a couple of days before the scan is done," Banerjee said.
Doctors said Mother Teresa had a bruise above her left eyebrow but there was no cause for concern.
Dr S.K. Sen, medical director at Calcutta's Woodlands Nursing home, said Mother Teresa wanted to go home.
"Doctor, you have got one house to look after and I have got hundreds of houses to look after. I have lots of work to do. So why do you keep me tied here?" Sen quoted her as saying.
The missionary, known as the Saint of the Gutters for her devotion to the poor and destitute, was admitted to the same hospital on August 20 with heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia.
She was released 18 days later and told to rest in bed.
Mother Teresa was reading magazines such as "Inside the Vatican" brought by the nuns of the missionaries of charity, Sen said.
"Mother even advised a doctor who got conjunctivitis to treat his eye," Sen said.
